So the C++ MDS never creates a lock cache, never grants Dc/Dr, and kernel async create/unlink never happen: those operations always go synchronously to the MDS. The kernel falls back to a synchronous UNLINK at linux/fs/ceph/dir.c:1316. Independently, the PRIMARY_LINK rule (F-CAPS-040) would also block it for clients holding Fs/Fx on the directory (G2, code reading).

features.group: Lock caches, async directory operations and delegated inode numbers
features.name: Replay of unsafe and async creates after failover
features.summary: Creates that a client saw acknowledged (or sent async) are replayed after an MDS restart and recreate the same inode numbers.
features.description: During up:reconnect, Server::dispatch queues requests with CEPH_MDS_FLAG_REPLAY or CEPH_MDS_FLAG_ASYNC for clientreplay (requests of non-open sessions are dropped) and registers a non-zero head.ino of a not-completed request with add_replay_ino_alloc so rejoin does not try to open it. Completed REPLAY requests are answered from completed_requests with result 0 and the created ino in extra_bl (no trace); a retried completed CREATE is re-dispatched as an open of the created inode. A not-completed replayed or async create re-executes and recreates the same ino from the session's prealloc set (all free after restart), reattaching the reconnected cap (try_reconnect_cap). REPLAY requests never early-reply and get no trace; requests queued for replay get no new caps beyond a reconnected one and no new delegations. With mds_replay_unsafe_with_closed_session such requests of sessions that did not reconnect are still replayed; their head.ino is moved from free to delegated so it is released rather than purged and reallocated from the InoTable.
features.notes: Completed-request tables and clientreplay are owned by 04-namespace-and-posix-operations and 01-cluster-membership-and-ha; this entry covers the client-named inode number part. The kernel resends unsafe requests with REPLAY and head.ino set and embedded releases stripped, then older unanswered requests (async ones keep ASYNC); libcephfs sets head.ino on replay too. See also F-CLU-095, F-CLU-084.

features.name: Per-object lock catalogue
features.summary: The fixed set of metadata locks on every inode and dentry and the metadata slice each protects.
features.description: Each dentry has lock (DN 1, simplelock: name linkage, leases) and versionlock (DVERSION 2, local). Each inode has quiescelock (IQUIESCE 16, local), snaplock (ISNAP 32: snaprealm), policylock (IPOLICY 64: layout, quota, export pins, flags, optmetadata), filelock (IFILE 128, filelock table: size, times, layout, client_ranges, inline data, dirstat, F caps), nestlock (INEST 256, scatter: rstat), dirfragtreelock (IDFT 512, scatter: fragment tree), authlock (IAUTH 1024: mode, uid, gid, fscrypt_auth; A caps), linklock (ILINK 2048: nlink; L caps), xattrlock (IXATTR 4096: xattrs; X caps), flocklock (IFLOCK 8192: fcntl/flock tables) and versionlock (IVERSION 16384, local). The numeric value is the per-object acquisition order. Each lock's protected fields are carried to replicas in encode_lock_state payloads. Lock states are never journaled or stored in RADOS.
features.notes: Granularity: filelock lumps size, mtime, atime, layout, client ranges, inline data, dirstat and all file caps, a source of false conflicts (lock-types page section 6). Dead or unimplemented machinery (staging lock-states:34): sm_t.careful/gcaps_careful/get_caps_careful, SimpleLock::req_rdlock_from_auth, ScatterLock::can_scatter_pin, SimpleLock::do_import, eval_scatter_gathers, the sender of LOCK_AC_REQUNSCATTER, LOCK_AC_FOR_*, MLock::reqid, LOCK_REMOTEXLOCK, LOCK_LOCK_MIX (declared only, yet it shifts every later state number), the TSYN family and file_recover's replica message. doc/dev/mds_internals/locking.rst is incomplete and partly wrong (no IQUIESCE, wrong LOCK semantics).

legacy_parts.note: The dead machinery listed in the notes: the sm_t careful column with SimpleLock::gcaps_careful and CInode::get_caps_careful (no caller), SimpleLock::req_rdlock_from_auth, ScatterLock::can_scatter_pin, SimpleLock::do_import and Locker::eval_scatter_gathers (no callers), the LOCK_AC_REQUNSCATTER handler (no sender), the LOCK_AC_FOR_REPLICA/LOCK_AC_FOR_AUTH macros (unused), MLock::reqid (never set), the LOCK_REMOTEXLOCK row (never assigned), LOCK_LOCK_MIX (declared only), the TSYN states and file_recover's replica LOCK message (commented out). None of the listed items has a caller, sender or assignment at this commit, so no peer can reach them. scatter_tempsync aborts on entry and its only call site in _rdlock_kick is commented out, so no lock reaches a TSYN state. LOCK_LOCK_MIX still shifts the numbers of all later lock states, which cross ranks only in C++ MDS-to-MDS encodings.
evidence_notes: search: grep -rn over src/mds and src/messages finds only definitions, table rows or name strings for get_caps_careful, req_rdlock_from_auth, can_scatter_pin, do_import, eval_scatter_gathers, LOCK_AC_FOR_*, set_reqid, LOCK_REMOTEXLOCK and LOCK_LOCK_MIX, and no sender of LOCK_AC_REQUNSCATTER

features.name: SimpleLock state machine (sm_simplelock)
features.summary: Shared-read / exclusive-write state machine used by most inode locks and the dentry lock.
features.description: Used by DN, IAUTH, ILINK, IXATTR, ISNAP, IFLOCK and IPOLICY. Stable states: SYNC (rdlock on auth and replicas, leases, s caps, replicas issue s), LOCK (no rdlock or wrlock; waypoint to an xlock), EXCL (the loner gets sx; the loner's requests may wrlock). Transitional: SYNC_LOCK, LOCK_SYNC, EXCL_SYNC, EXCL_LOCK, SYNC_EXCL, LOCK_EXCL, SNAP_SYNC; xlock path LOCK -> LOCK_XLOCK -> PREXLOCK -> XLOCK -> XLOCKDONE, returning to SYNC. Primitives simple_sync, simple_lock, simple_excl, simple_xlock. Replicas only hold SYNC, SYNC_LOCK and LOCK. It is the only class that can be xlocked remotely. allowed_ever_auth s|x, allowed_ever_replica s.
features.notes: The LOCK_REMOTEXLOCK row is never assigned (a remote xlock leaves the replica in LOCK). _finish_xlock also puts flocklock (no caps) into EXCL when the xlocker is the target loner; simple_eval then syncs it back.

legacy_parts.note: The LOCK_REMOTEXLOCK row of the simplelock table, which no code assigns. grep over src/mds finds LOCK_REMOTEXLOCK only in the enum, the simplelock table row and the state-name switch, so no lock enters that state. A remote xlock leaves the replica in LOCK. The rest of sm_simplelock is live.

features.name: ScatterLock state machine (nestlock, dirfragtreelock)
features.summary: State machine for metadata that several ranks update concurrently and the inode auth periodically sums.
features.description: Stable: SYNC (readable everywhere, unwritable), LOCK (auth-only wrlock, unreadable), MIX (wrlock on every rank, unreadable). Transitions SYNC_LOCK, LOCK_SYNC, SYNC_MIX/SYNC_MIX2, MIX_SYNC, MIX_LOCK/MIX_LOCK2 (two-stage: replicas are messaged only after the local stage), SNAP_SYNC; LOCK -> MIX happens directly without a gather. scatter_eval keeps a replicated nestlock in MIX and an unreplicated one in LOCK ("keep INEST writable at all times"); dirfragtreelock goes to SYNC unless the inode has subtree-root or exporting dirfrags. No caps are ever issued for these locks. The TSYN (temp-sync) family is unimplemented (scatter_tempsync aborts).
features.notes: Undefined rows (code reading): replicas of nestlock/dirfragtreelock are put into MIX_SYNC2, which has no row in scatterlock[] (all-zero: stable with no permissions) until the auth's AC_SYNC arrives; the table allows xlock in LOCK but has no XLOCK rows, reachable only through the `lock path` admin command, which then reaches ceph_abort() (lock-types page section 8 item 1).

legacy_parts.note: The TSYN (temp-sync) family: the TSYN_LOCK, TSYN, LOCK_TSYN, MIX_TSYN and TSYN_MIX rows of the scatterlock table, Locker::scatter_tempsync, and the TSYN branches in simple_sync, simple_lock, scatter_mix, eval_gather and handle_file_lock. scatter_tempsync aborts before it sets any TSYN state, and its only call site in _rdlock_kick is commented out, so no lock reaches a TSYN state. The TSYN branches elsewhere test states that never occur. The SYNC, LOCK and MIX machinery of the entry is live.

features.name: FileLock state machine (sm_filelock)
features.summary: State machine of filelock, combining scatter states with loner, xlock, snapshot and recovery states; it decides all F caps.
features.description: Stable: SYNC (everyone Fscrl, replicas Fscr), LOCK (auth wrlock only; clients keep Fcb), MIX (wrlock on every rank; clients Frwl, replicas Fr), EXCL (loner Fsxcrwb; nobody else gets file caps), XSYN (loner keeps Fcb; the auth may rdlock). Transitional *_SYNC, *_LOCK, *_MIX, *_EXCL, *_XSYN states; xlock states (an XLOCK returns to LOCK, unlike simplelock); XLOCKSNAP; PRE_SCAN/SCAN (size recovery). On directories it also scatter-gathers dirstat. Primitives file_excl, scatter_mix, file_xsyn, file_recover, simple_sync, simple_lock, simple_xlock. allowed_ever_auth is all eight bits, allowed_ever_replica s|c|r|l.
features.notes: scatter_mix from LOCK does not gather: it sets MIX immediately, so clients may still hold Fc/Fb (allowed in LOCK, not in MIX) while the revocation is in flight (lock-types page section 8 item 26). Fa is never issued; Fl only in the SYNC/MIX family.

features.name: XSYN: rdlock while a loner keeps buffered data
features.summary: filelock state that lets the auth read a file's metadata while its exclusive writer keeps its page cache and buffers.
features.description: When a request on the auth rdlocks a regular file's filelock that is in EXCL with a target loner (not anonymous, not a directory), _rdlock_kick calls file_xsyn (EXCL -> EXCL_XSYN -> XSYN) instead of simple_sync: the loner keeps Fcb and loses Fs/Fx/Fr/Fw, the auth may rdlock, and the loner's requests may still wrlock. file_eval later leaves XSYN (file_excl accepts XSYN as a source).
features.notes: Example: another client stats a file that the loner is writing, on the auth rank (lock-types page section 3.13).

features.name: Local locks (versionlock, quiescelock)
features.summary: Rank-local locks that are never replicated, used for projected-version pipelining and the quiesce barrier.
features.description: LocalLockC is always in LOCK and is never replicated, carried in MLock or evaluated. wrlocks are shared; an xlock excludes wrlocks; a queued xlocker blocks new wrlockers (can_wrlock = not xlocked and no WAIT_XLOCK waiter). rdlock is never used (asserted). local_xlock_start invalidates lock caches holding the lock; local_xlock_finish wakes waiters and, for quiescelock, re-evaluates the inode's cap locks with caps_imported so blocked requests run before caps are re-issued. versionlock's last_wrlock_client decides projected-value visibility in replies.
features.notes: See also F-QOS-045 (quiescelock use).

features.name: Gather engine (eval_gather) and cap revocation gather
features.summary: The completion test for lock transitions: a lock stays in its transitional state until every conflicting holder, client cap, lease and replica has let go.
features.description: A transition primitive sets the transitional state, revokes conflicting caps (issued_caps_need_gather compares issued bits with the transitional state's columns), revokes leases, messages replicas and auth-pins the parent. eval_gather completes the transition when: no replica ack is outstanding; each held rdlock/wrlock/xlock/lease is permitted (ANY, or AUTH on the auth) by the next state; no scatter writebehind is in flight; no issued (not just pending) loner/other/xlocker cap bit exceeds the next state's columns; the state is not SYNC_MIX2/MIX_SYNC2; and (filelock) no file recovery is pending. Replicas then send LOCKACK/MIXACK/SYNCACK; the auth runs the two-stage MIX_LOCK, a writebehind, or start_scatter + AC_MIX / AC_SYNC with data; finally it sets the next state, auth-unpins, may drop the loner, wakes WAIT_STABLE|WAIT_WR|WAIT_RD|WAIT_XLOCK waiters, calls try_eval and issues caps. Triggers: the last rdlock/wrlock/xlock released, cap ack/flush/release, snapflush completion, stale forced revoke, last lease released or expired, replica acks, recovery completion.
features.notes: Client acks are on the critical path of every conflicting operation, and there is no lock-level timeout. Transitional columns define what clients keep during a transition (e.g. filelock EXCL_SYNC keeps Fscr for the loner while Fx|Fw|Fb are revoked).

features.name: Lock-mode grant rules (rdlock / wrlock / xlock compatibility)
features.summary: Which lock modes can be held together, derived from the permission columns of the current state.
features.description: There is no static compatibility matrix: a mode is grantable when the current state's column allows it: ANY (auth or replica), AUTH (auth only), XCL (only the client recorded as xlocker; for wrlock and force-wrlock also the loner excl_client), REQ (never here; a replica asks the auth), 0 (never). Consequences: readers need SYNC (or XSYN/TSYN on the auth), writers need LOCK, MIX or loner states, so rdlocks and wrlocks of different clients never coexist except filelock XSYN; wrlocks are shared counters; there is one active xlocker; after an early reply (XLOCKDONE) the xlocking client may rdlock, lease, read projected values and start the next xlock (except on filelock, tracker 49132); in EXCL the loner's requests may wrlock without a transition.
features.notes: POSIX atomicity of namespace operations (rename, link, create) relies on these exclusions together with the lock sets each handler declares.

features.name: Lock-request-driven state changes and journal nudging
features.summary: How rdlock, wrlock and xlock requests kick lock transitions, and why waiting on a lock flushes the journal.
features.description: rdlock_start: if not grantable, _rdlock_kick on a stable auth lock (simple_sync, or file_xsyn for a buffering loner) or LOCK_AC_REQRDLOCK from a replica; waits WAIT_RD (auth, stable) or WAIT_STABLE; snapshot reads use the anonymous client. wrlock_start: grants if can_wrlock and, when the inode has subtree-root/exporting dirfrags or scatter_wanted, the state is MIX; otherwise scatter_mix or simple_lock on the auth, LOCK_AC_REQSCATTER from a replica; waits WAIT_STABLE. xlock_start: on the auth moves LOCK (or the same client's XLOCKDONE) to LOCK_XLOCK via simple_xlock, other stable states first to LOCK; grants when this request started the xlock and can_xlock holds; replicas of simple locks request a remote xlock. Every wait calls nudge_log, which flushes the MDLog when the lock is auth, unstable, locked and has waiters, because holders of early-replied mutations release only at journal commit; simple_sync with wrlocks and the replica MLock handlers flush too. Requests on a recovering filelock prioritize its file recovery.

features.name: Scatter data exchange and writebehind
features.summary: Lock-side protocol that collects per-dirfrag deltas from all ranks into the inode and journals the result.
features.description: For filelock on directories (dirstat), nestlock (rstat) and dirfragtreelock (fragment tree), dirfrag auths accumulate deltas while the lock is MIX and the inode auth sums them on gather. Replicas acking MIX_LOCK or MIX_SYNC send encode_lock_ifile/inest/idft of their auth fragments with a dirty flag and start_flush; the auth marks the lock dirty when data is pending. A dirty unflushed lock makes eval_gather run scatter_writebehind: forced wrlock, project the inode with a new version, finish_scatter_gather_update (sum deltas with version epochs, validate, clamp negatives), FLUSHING, journal EUpdate("scatter_writebehind") and flush; on commit: apply, FLUSHED, unpin PIN_DIRTYSCATTERED, leave the LogSegment dirty list, send LOCK_AC_LOCKFLUSHED to replicas in MIX_LOCK/MIX_LOCK2/MIX_EXCL, drop the wrlock to continue the gather. For dirfragtreelock replicas send their tree and auth frags and the auth forces those frags to leaves. Replicas receiving AC_MIX/AC_SYNC data journal accounted-stat resyncs for their lagging fragments.
features.notes: What dirstat and rstat count, their eager propagation in predirty_journal_parents and their freshness are owned by 08-snapshots-quotas-subvolumes; dirfrag split/merge by 05-metadata-cache-and-dirfrags. Mismatches are logged ("unmatched fragstat", "inconsistent rstat") and repaired by trusting the fragments; they are fatal only with mds_verify_scatter (dev). "Marking stale" is only a log message. See also F-SNAP-037 (what the gather sums), F-CACHE-091 (fragtree propagation).

features.name: Scatter nudging
features.summary: Periodic and journal-driven forcing of dirty scatterlocks so deferred statistics get summed and journal segments can be trimmed.
features.description: mark_updated_scatterlock appends a dirty lock to Locker::updated_scatterlocks with a timestamp. scatter_tick, from Locker::tick every mds_tick_interval (5 s) on clientreplay/active/stopping ranks (not while the beacon is laggy), nudges locks older than mds_scatter_nudge_interval (5 s) and flushes the journal. scatter_nudge on the auth moves a replicated non-MIX lock to MIX, else a non-LOCK lock to LOCK, else to SYNC (at most two cycles), waiting if frozen or unstable; on a replica it sends LOCK_AC_NUDGE. LogSegment::try_to_expire nudges every inode on the segment's dirty_dirfrag_* lists, so a segment cannot be trimmed until its scattered data is written behind.
features.notes: scatter_tick stops at the first entry younger than the interval and requeued entries keep their old stamp, so the list is not strictly ordered. On frozen or ambiguous-auth inodes without a context scatter_nudge just requeues ("not ideal.. starvation prone.."). See also F-SNAP-036 (deferred stat propagation), F-SNAP-038 (segment expiry waits for stat folding).

features.name: Inter-MDS lock protocol (MLock)
features.summary: MDS-to-MDS message that keeps replica lock states in step with the auth rank.
features.description: MSG_MDS_LOCK (0x300, v1): asker, action, reqid (never set), lock_type, MDSCacheObjectInfo {ino, dirfrag, dname, snapid}, lockdata. Auth -> replicas: SYNC (-1), MIX (-2), LOCK (-3), LOCKFLUSHED (-4); replica -> auth: SYNCACK (1), MIXACK (2), LOCKACK (3), REQSCATTER (7), REQUNSCATTER (8, never sent), NUDGE (9), REQRDLOCK (10). Only the auth initiates state changes; replicas follow and ack after their local gathers. send_lock_message skips ranks below REJOIN while the cluster is degraded, yet init_gather adds all replicas to the gather set. Messages for objects not in cache are dropped; while the receiver is in rejoin, messages for rejoining objects are dropped and never retransmitted.
features.notes: MDS-to-MDS only (ALLOW_MESSAGES_FROM MDS); never seen by clients, monitors or OSDs. handle_simple_lock ignores unknown actions; handle_file_lock aborts on them. A gather including a rank below REJOIN finishes only when that rank rejoins.

legacy_parts.note: LOCK_AC_REQUNSCATTER (8): handle_file_lock has a case for it, but no code sends it. MLock::reqid: encoded and decoded in every MLock but never set. grep over src/mds finds LOCK_AC_REQUNSCATTER only in locks.h, the action-name switch and the handle_file_lock case, and finds no caller of MLock::set_reqid. MLock is exchanged only between C++ MDS ranks. The other actions are live.

features.name: Replica-initiated lock state requests
features.summary: Replica ranks ask the auth rank to change a lock state so they can rdlock or wrlock locally.
features.description: A replica that cannot rdlock sends LOCK_AC_REQRDLOCK; the auth (if not SYNC and not frozen) runs simple_sync on a stable lock or retries the message once the lock is stable, else drops it (the replica waits on its own WAIT_STABLE). A replica that cannot wrlock sends LOCK_AC_REQSCATTER; the auth runs scatter_mix on a stable lock (even while freezing, since the requester holds an auth pin) or sets scatter_wanted on an unstable one. Replicas send LOCK_AC_NUDGE from scatter_nudge. Requesters hold remote auth pins so the auth cannot freeze meanwhile.
features.notes: handle_reqrdlock's unfreeze wait is ineffective: SimpleLock::add_waiter shifts WAIT_UNFREEZE into the lock-waiter half, so only WAIT_STABLE wakes it (lock-types page section 8 item 28). A REQSCATTER that reaches the auth in MIX_SYNC sets scatter_wanted, so the auth scatters again right after reaching SYNC (code reading).

features.name: Lock state across replication, migration and rejoin
features.summary: Encodings and rules that carry lock states between ranks when objects are replicated, exported, renamed across ranks or recovered.
features.description: New replicas receive each lock's replica_state (bare s16; NEED_RECOVER if created while the auth recovers). Export sends SimpleLock::encode (state + gather_set) for nine inode locks plus loner_cap and the dentry lock, and export_twiddle turns the exporter's copy into replica state; during export the exporter holds lock_scatter_gather (WRLOCK|STATE_PIN) on the exported dirfrag inode's filelock and nestlock; the importer re-marks dirty scatterlocks and re-evaluates snaplock/policylock. In rename inode migration xlock_export converts xlocks to replica LOCK and xlock_import re-pins them on the importer. Rejoin: survivors report scatter states (MIX_SYNC/MIX_LOCK while the recovering rank is in the gather set, NEED_RECOVER for MIX*), the recovering auth infers MIX (or LOCK for non-directory filelocks) and re-creates survivors' xlocks/wrlocks; rdlocks on NEED_RECOVER locks wait for cluster recovery. Replica DN locks mirror the auth (LOCK is not readable, so replica path traversal waits WAIT_RD); the DN payload carries linkage but replicas only adopt first, and linkage changes travel in MDentryLink/MDentryUnlink.
features.notes: Raw state numbers (implicit locks.h enum) cross ranks only in these encodings. Server::_rename_apply and _commit_peer_rename iterate mdr->locks from &in->versionlock, relying on CInode member layout (acquiring-locks page section 8). Recovery stages are owned by 01-cluster-membership-and-ha and subtree export by 07-multi-mds.

features.name: acquire_locks and lock vectors
features.summary: The main entry point through which requests declare and obtain their locks without ever blocking a thread.
features.description: Callers build a LockOpVec (RDLOCK 1, WRLOCK 2, XLOCK 4, REMOTE_WRLOCK 8 with a target rank, STATE_PIN 16) in the order the locks must be taken across objects. acquire_locks(mdr, lov, auth_pin_freeze, auth_pin_nonblocking, skip_quiesce): pass 1 adds implicit locks (versionlock, quiescelock) and collects objects to pin; sort_and_merge; check pinnability of all objects (dropping everything and waiting on WAIT_UNFREEZE or WAIT_SINGLEAUTH if one is not pinnable, or aborting with auth_pin_nonblocking); take local auth pins; send OP_AUTHPIN to other ranks and return; then acquire each lock in order, skipping held ones. On the first lock that is not grantable it registers a waiter and returns false, keeping the locks already held (partial holds). Held locks live in MutationImpl::locks, a set ordered by lock address.
features.notes: Every client metadata operation goes through it. Other acquisition paths: try_rdlock_snap_layout, rdlock_try_set, wrlock_try, wrlock_force / local_wrlock_grab and lock caches. A merged RDLOCK|WRLOCK entry loses the rdlock (no current caller). Release iterates in address order and may synchronously run other requests' handlers.

features.name: Per-object lock order
features.summary: Locks on the same object are always taken in ascending lock-type order.
features.description: sort_and_merge sorts each consecutive run of entries on the same object by CEPH_LOCK_* value (DN < DVERSION; IQUIESCE < ISNAP < IPOLICY < IFILE < INEST < IDFT < IAUTH < ILINK < IXATTR < IFLOCK < IVERSION) and merges adjacent entries for the same lock by OR-ing flags; an XLOCK replaces all other modes. Within one call the implicit quiescelock is therefore first on its inode and versionlock last.
features.notes: Entries for one object that are not adjacent in the caller's vector are neither sorted together nor merged (a convention, not checked).

features.name: Cross-object ordering rules and no upgrades
features.summary: Deadlock-avoidance rules for locks on different objects.
features.description: O1 caller order across objects; O3 path components top-down (parent directory locks, dentry, child snaplock), one acquire_locks per step; O4 two-path operations order directory inodes and dentries: objects under the fs root before those under ~mdsN, then by depth, then by directory ino, dentries in one directory by name, non-directory inodes by ino; O5 target-inode locks after the path, stray locks last; O7 no upgrades (a request never xlocks a lock it rdlocked in an earlier call; code that needs a read-only check first drops its locks); O8 a later call must not add a lock that sorts before one already held on the same object, except the implicit quiescelock, which is safe because its failure drops everything. Violations show up as deadlocks, not errors; e.g. getattr restarts the request if its filelock decision changes between retries.
features.notes: Deadlock freedom of rename and link depends on these rules (commit 246f647566 introduced the two-path ordering). doc/dev/mds_internals/locking.rst ends with "TODO: Explain locking order and path traversal locking."

features.name: Ancestor snaplock/policylock try-rdlocks and layout inheritance
features.summary: Bottom-up, try-only read locks on every ancestor's snapshot and policy locks, which also supply the inherited file layout.
features.description: try_rdlock_snap_layout walks from the request's base inode to the root rdlocking each snaplock (stopping at one already held) and, with want_layout, each policylock until an ancestor whose projected inode has a layout, copying that layout into mdr->dir_layout for new files. It takes locks only when immediately grantable, without kicking and without auth pins (so it works on replicas and does not block freezes); on the first failure it drops all locks and local auth pins and waits WAIT_RD. It records dir_root and dir_depth used for two-path ordering. Ancestor snap/policy rdlocks are held until the safe reply (they survive the early reply), so mksnap, setlayout and quota changes anywhere above wait for unsafe requests below.
features.notes: It inserts directly into mdr->locks without updating last_locked. Operations that xlock snaplock/policylock take the xlock on their target first and then try-rdlock the parent ancestry.

features.name: Path traversal locking and path helpers
features.summary: Locking flags of MDCache::path_traverse and the Server helpers that lock a path for an operation.
features.description: path_traverse takes per-component locks according to flags: RDLOCK_SNAP/SNAP2 (ancestor try-rdlocks, child snaplocks), RDLOCK_PATH (rdlock each dentry; also wrlock the parent filelock when another client's lock cache holds it), XLOCK_DENTRY (tail: wrlock parent filelock + nestlock, optional RDLOCK_AUTHLOCK, xlock the dentry), CHECK_LOCKCACHE, WANT_DIRLAYOUT, PATH_LOCKED (peers do not wait on unreadable dentries). Waits inside traversal drop all locks; without RDLOCK_PATH an unreadable dentry makes the traversal wait WAIT_RD (counter traverse_lock). Helpers: rdlock_path_pin_ref (inode ops; auth-pins the target and refuses a freezing target it has not pinned), rdlock_path_xlock_dentry (create/unlink style; EEXIST/ENOENT checks), rdlock_two_paths_xlock_destdn (rename and link: both paths depth 1, ordered per F-CAPS-077, remote wrlocks for a source dirfrag on another rank, auth_pin_freeze for a non-auth primary source), xlock_policylock (xlock policylock (+snaplock) then try-rdlock the parent ancestry). PATH_LOCKED and ALL_LOCKED make retries idempotent.
features.notes: Path resolution, forwarding and discover are owned by 05-metadata-cache-and-dirfrags; per-operation lock sets are listed in the acquiring-locks worked examples. See also F-NS-005 (request-side helpers), F-CACHE-041 (path_traverse).

features.name: Implicit versionlock (pipelining and peer rollback)
features.summary: versionlock is added automatically next to every xlock, shared on the leader and exclusive on a peer.
features.description: For an xlock on an auth dentry lock the leader adds a wrlock on the dentry's versionlock and a peer adds an xlock; for an xlock on an inode lock other than IVERSION/IQUIESCE on an auth inode the leader adds a versionlock wrlock and a peer an xlock. Leader wrlocks are shared and let several projected updates of one object pipeline into the journal; a peer's xlock blocks every other journaled update of that object until the cross-rank operation ends ("this makes rollback safe"). setattr that sets ctime also wrlocks versionlock; predirty_journal_parents grabs ancestor versionlocks with local_wrlock_grab.

features.name: Implicit quiescelock wrlock
features.summary: Lock-acquisition side of the implicit quiescelock wrlock.
features.description: See F-QOS-045. Lock-acquisition specifics: the implicit wrlock is added in Locker::acquire_locks right after the first xlock, wrlock or remote wrlock on a cap-bearing inode lock (authlock, linklock, filelock, xattrlock) of the call, at most one per call; when the quiescelock is unavailable, handle_quiesce_failure drops all locks and local auth pins, sends OP_FINISH to all peers and waits, so no request waits on a quiesced inode while holding path locks. Fragmentation does not pass skip_quiesce.
features.notes: Only one quiescelock is added per call: a two-directory rename gates only the first-ordered parent directory and one of srci/oldin (whether quiesce relies on more is undocumented; unverified). Lock caches hold the parent directory's quiescelock wrlock on behalf of async dirops. Policy vxattrs take no quiescelock, but their policylock xlock waits on quiesce_inode's policylock rdlock. See also F-CAPS-066 (local locks).

features.name: Local auth pins on locked objects
features.summary: Every lock taken through acquire_locks on an auth object also pins the object against freezing (export, fragmentation, rename migration).
features.description: Every non-local lock taken through acquire_locks on an auth object, including plain rdlocks, requires an auth pin; on a replica the object is (remotely) pinned only when the lock may have to be requested from the auth. Pinnability of all objects of a call is checked before any lock of that call: an inode is pinnable if auth, not freezing/frozen and its dirfrag is pinnable; a dirfrag if auth and not in a freezing/frozen dir or tree. Failure drops everything and waits WAIT_UNFREEZE (events such as "failed to authpin, subtree is being exported"). Local-lock wrlocks and try_rdlock_snap_layout rdlocks take no pin; unstable locks hold their own auth pin, so freezes also wait for pending lock transitions.
features.notes: See also F-CACHE-028 (auth pin accounting).

features.name: Remote auth pins and the rename frozen auth pin
features.summary: Pinning objects whose authority is another rank, including the special freeze of a renamed inode.
features.description: For objects whose auth is another rank the leader sends MMDSPeerRequest OP_AUTHPIN (3) with the complete set of objects at that rank, an optional authpin_freeze (carried in the object_info field), and FLAG_NONBLOCKING or FLAG_NOTIFYBLOCKING. The peer fails with FLAG_EROFS on a read-only fs or FLAG_WOULDBLOCK for nonblocking requests, or waits for unfreeze (sending FLAG_REQBLOCKED if asked, so the leader drops its locks and keeps waiting), then pins everything and replies OP_AUTHPINACK (-3) with its full pinned list; EROFS/WOULDBLOCK become -EROFS/-EAGAIN for the leader. For a rename whose source dentry is not auth and is a primary link, the source inode's auth freeze_auth_pins it (auth pin, freeze_inode(1), STATE_FROZENAUTHPIN) so nobody can auth-pin it between lock acquisition and rename prep (ABBA deadlock). Several OP_AUTHPIN requests (one per rank) may be outstanding.
features.notes: A peer lacking the object or not its auth replies with an empty pin list and no error; the leader recomputes authority. handle_peer_auth_pin_ack is the only place that clears remote_auth_pinned records, so after a quiesce failure stale pin records survive (acquiring-locks page section 8; impact on the rename frozen pin unverified).

features.name: Remote xlocks and remote wrlocks
features.summary: Taking an exclusive or shared write lock on another rank's authoritative copy of an object.
features.description: A leader xlocks a simple lock (DN, IAUTH, ILINK, IXATTR, ISNAP, IFLOCK, IPOLICY) of a non-auth object with OP_XLOCK (1); the auth runs acquire_locks(skip_quiesce) on its peer request (so the object's versionlock is xlocked), stays in XLOCK (peers never early-reply) and answers OP_XLOCKACK (-1) carrying encode_locked_state; the leader's replica stays in LOCK and records the xlock; OP_UNXLOCK (2) releases it. Cross-rank rename and link remote-wrlock the source directory's filelock/nestlock at the source dirfrag's auth with OP_WRLOCK (8) / OP_WRLOCKACK (-8) / OP_UNWRLOCK (9); when a local wrlock on the same lock is also needed it is taken with wrlock_try, and on failure the remote wrlock is released and re-requested so the gather can finish. Remote locks are obtained one round trip at a time, each followed by a full re-dispatch; a non-auth OP_XLOCK is dropped without reply.
features.notes: set_xlocks_done asserts every xlocked object is auth; this holds because remote xlocks are only taken by link/unlink/rename flows whose journaled peers suppress the early reply (inferred, not asserted). MMDSPeerRequest is MDS-to-MDS only (HEAD_VERSION = COMPAT_VERSION = 1).

features.name: Remote lock teardown and peer failure
features.summary: Releasing locks held on other ranks and handling a peer rank that fails mid-request.
features.description: _drop_locks sends OP_DROPLOCKS (11) to every rank where remote xlocks or wrlocks were held (if it is at least up:rejoin); the peer drops the locks but keeps its auth pins and peer request. request_drop_remote_locks sends OP_FINISH (17), with FLAG_ABORT when the leader was killed before committing, to every rank in more()->peers, forgets foreign xlocks and remote wrlocks locally and clears peers. When a peer rank fails, non-committing leader requests drop it from waiting_on_peer, forget an in-flight remote lock aimed at it and retry when it is active; peer requests from a failed leader without a prepare are aborted or finished, and prepared ones wait for resolve.
features.notes: Resolve of prepared peer updates is owned by 01-cluster-membership-and-ha. A killed request waiting on peers is only marked aborted and finishes when the peer replies.

features.name: FIFO lock waiters with synchronous wake-up
features.summary: Waiters on a lock are woken in arrival order, inside the call stack that released or stabilized the lock.
features.description: Lock waiter bits (WAIT_RD 1, WAIT_WR 2, WAIT_XLOCK = WAIT_STABLE 4, WAIT_REMOTEXLOCK 8) are shifted into the upper half of each cache object's 128-bit wait mask (bit 64 + a 4-bit slot per lock type) and always added with WAIT_ORDERED, which gives a global increasing sequence; take_waiting returns them in sequence order and finish_contexts completes them synchronously in the caller's stack (e.g. inside eval_gather or another request's _drop_locks); unordered waiters (unfreeze, single auth) get sequence 0 and run first. A woken request that fails again re-queues behind newer waiters.
features.notes: Head-of-line blocking: a transitional state blocks all new incompatible requests, so one xlock waiter stalls later readers even while it waits for an unresponsive client. See also F-CACHE-033 (waiter queues on cache objects).

features.name: Non-blocking lock helpers
features.summary: Lock primitives that never wait, used where waiting is not allowed or a lock must be held regardless of state.
features.description: rdlock_try (check with one kick, take nothing); rdlock_try_set (take a set of rdlocks, or register WAIT_STABLE|WAIT_RD and drop everything; used by export); wrlock_try (take if grantable, else simple_lock only if stable, auth, clean, not scatter_wanted and without subtree dirfrags, never starting a scatter or writebehind because the caller may have a log entry open); wrlock_force (take regardless of state, for locks held during a journal write: cap updates, max_size, export, fragmentation, rstat propagation, writebehind); local_wrlock_grab (assert and grant).
features.notes: rdlock_try_set with a lock already rdlocked by the request would leak one rdlock reference (no current caller does so).

features.name: Freeze versus auth-pin deadlock breaker
features.summary: Timeout that cancels an export or fragmentation whose freeze is stuck behind requests holding remote auth pins.
features.description: A request that holds a remote auth pin and must wait on a freezing object calls notify_freeze_waiter, incrementing num_remote_waiters of the fragmentation or of the export rooted at the freezing tree. Each MDSRankDispatcher::tick on an active rank runs find_stale_fragment_freeze and find_stale_export_freeze: if a freeze's cumulative auth-pin count did not change for mds_freeze_tree_timeout and there are remote waiters (or the parent directory is also freezing), the fragmentation or export is cancelled. The peer side does the same when an OP_AUTHPIN must wait.
features.notes: Export and fragmentation themselves are owned by 07-multi-mds and 05-metadata-cache-and-dirfrags. notify_freeze_waiter is called from acquire_locks, rdlock_path_pin_ref, repair_dirfrag_stats_work and Server::handle_peer_auth_pin. Cancelled fragment operations are not re-queued. dump_export_states shows last_cum_auth_pins, last_cum_auth_pins_change and num_remote_waiters for DISCOVERING/FREEZING exports. See also F-MULTI-024 (export side), F-CACHE-029 and F-CACHE-030 (freezing).

features.name: Lock waits on a degraded cluster
features.summary: Locks that wait for cluster recovery while some rank is failed or recovering.
features.description: While the cluster is degraded: an xlock on ISNAP or IPOLICY by a leader not queued for replay drops locks and local pins and waits for cluster recovery if the (auth) object has a replica on a rank below active, or the (non-auth) lock is not yet xlocked ("to guarantee replayed requests and mksnap/setlayout get processed in proper order"); an rdlock on a NEED_RECOVER lock drops locks (keeping local pins) and waits unless the request is a queued replay (when not degraded the flag is simply cleared); remote lock and auth-pin requests wait for the peer to be clientreplay, active or stopping; lock messages to ranks below up:rejoin are skipped.
features.notes: See also F-CLU-091.

features.name: xlock lifecycle
features.summary: How an exclusive lock is obtained on the auth, held across the journal write and released.
features.description: xlock_start drives LOCK_XLOCK -> PREXLOCK (gathered) -> XLOCK with get_xlock(mdr, client) (one xlock_by mutation, num_xlock, xlock_by_client). When the request finishes, xlock_finish calls put_xlock; at num_xlock == 0 _finish_xlock either jumps straight to EXCL (lock types other than DN/ISNAP/IPOLICY, with no rdlocks, wrlocks or leases, not XLOCKSNAP, when the xlocker is the inode's target loner or anonymous), skipping a SYNC round trip, or runs eval_gather to the table's next state (SYNC for simple locks, sending LOCK_AC_SYNC with the new value to replicas; LOCK for filelock). cancel_locking handles a request dropping an in-flight xlock (PREXLOCK -> _finish_xlock; LOCK_XLOCK -> XLOCKDONE then eval_gather).

features.name: XLOCKDONE: read-your-own-unsafe-writes
features.summary: Between the unsafe and the safe reply, the client that made a change may already use it while other clients wait for durability.
features.description: At an early (unsafe) reply set_xlocks_done moves every xlock of the request to XLOCKDONE and clears xlock_by but keeps xlock_by_client (rename keeps its dentry xlocks in LOCK_XLOCK so dentries with projected linkage get no new replicas). In XLOCKDONE the same client may read, rdlock, take a lease, read projected values, hold xlocker_caps (s) and start its next xlock (pipelining; disabled for filelock, tracker 49132, so back-to-back size/mtime setattrs serialize on the journal), while other clients wait until the request is safe. encode_inodestat shows projected inode fields only to the client that xlocks the corresponding lock or is the loner (versionlock: the last wrlocking client), and projected dentry linkage only to the xlocking client or request. Early reply is skipped (one safe reply, journal flushed immediately) when mds_early_reply is false, no_early_reply is set (SETDIRLAYOUT and the ceph.dir.layout, ceph.quota, ceph.quiesce.block, ceph.dir.subvolume, ceph.dir.subvolume.snaps.visible vxattrs), peers journaled, an ino was allocated from the InoTable, or the request came from an MDS or is a replay.
features.notes: The kclient completes the syscall on the first reply and keeps the request until the safe reply. Other clients do not observe another client's non-durable metadata through replies or caps; one exception found is MClientQuota, filled from the projected rstat (lock-types page section 7 item 4). The unsafe/safe reply protocol is owned by 04-namespace-and-posix-operations.

features.name: Early-reply rdlock release and journal flush policy
features.summary: Which locks an early-replied request gives up before its journal entry commits, and when the journal is flushed.
features.description: After submitting the journal entry of an early-replied request, Server::journal_and_reply calls handle_locks_for_early_reply: it releases every rdlock except snaplock and policylock rdlocks (kept "to make later mksnap/setlayout (at other mds) wait for this unsafe request") and flushes the journal once, only if a held auth lock is unstable, locked and has waiters. Without an early reply the log is flushed immediately; a request replayed after failover only queues the next replay op. Wrlocks and xlocks stay until the request is safe; anyone waiting on them triggers nudge_log.
features.notes: Determines how long other clients wait behind an unsafe request (journal commit latency).

features.name: Lock release at safe reply and cleanup
features.summary: Order in which a finished request gives up its locks, auth pins and lock-cache reference.
features.description: reply_client_request calls request_drop_non_rdlocks before building the safe reply ("drop non-rdlocks before replying, so that we can issue leases"): OP_FINISH to peers, then all xlocks, wrlocks and remote wrlocks, each release possibly waking and running waiting requests synchronously; the trace with leases and caps is included only if no unsafe reply was sent. request_cleanup then drops the remaining rdlocks and the lock-cache reference, local auth pins, runs kick_cap_releases and drops cache pins; request_forward and request_kill also clean up. drop_lock releases one held lock in whatever mode it is held (quiesce_inode sheds its cap locks once it holds the quiescelock); drop_locks_for_fragment_unfreeze releases everything except dirfragtreelock.

features.name: Cap and lease counters and dumps
features.summary: Perf counters and admin output describing caps, leases and delegated inodes.
features.description: Perf counters: mds.caps and mds.inodes_with_caps; mds_mem.cap, cap+, cap- (live, added and removed Capability objects); mds.handle_client_caps, handle_client_caps_dirty, handle_client_cap_release, process_request_cap_release, handle_inode_file_caps; mds.ceph_cap_op_grant, ceph_cap_op_revoke, ceph_cap_op_trunc, ceph_cap_op_flush_ack, ceph_cap_op_flushsnap_ack; mds_server.cap_revoke_eviction and cap_acquisition_throttle. No counter is dedicated to leases, lock caches or delegations. Admin: dump inode shows client_caps [{client_id, pending, issued, wanted, last_sent}], loner, want_loner and mds_caps_wanted; session ls / client ls show num_caps, num_leases, num_completed_flushes, recall/release counters, delegated_inos and prealloc_inos.
features.notes: mds_mem.cap is read by the mgr status module, the dashboard and telemetry. The perf-counter and admin-command frameworks are owned by 11-security-admin-and-observability.

features.name: Lock state dumps and lock-related op events
features.summary: Admin visibility into lock states and into why a request is waiting.
features.description: dump inode / dump cache print per lock gather_set, the state name (SimpleLock::get_state_name strings), type, is_leased, num_rdlocks, num_wrlocks, num_xlocks and xlock_by (SYNC unlocked locks are dumped empty); debug logs mark leased and cached locks. ops / dump_ops_in_flight / dump_blocked_ops show acquire_locks events ("failed to rdlock, waiting", "failed to xlock, waiting", "failed to authpin, subtree is being exported", "requesting remote authpins", "failed to acquire quiesce lock", "acquired locks"); ops flags=locks dumps each request's held locks {object, object_string, lock, flags, wrlock_target}. The lock path test command that takes arbitrary locks is F-ADM-053.
features.notes: There is no lock-state or lock-wait counter (only traverse_lock). QA tests consume the op event strings.
